newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up on market boost plans.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up on market boost plans.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B shares ended firmer on Thursday after an official newspaper said the city planned measures to boost the market, analysts said.
The B share index rose 0.91 points or 0.58 percent to end at 158.67, but turnover dipped to HK$64.56 million from HK$80.16 million on Wednesday.

The Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Thursday the city planned to set up a new stock data network in Hong Kong and would encourage more B share companies to obtain secondary listings on overseas bourses.
"The news has injected fresh confidence into the market because it shows Shenzhen is taking care of its market," an analyst with J & A Securities said.
Of the 44 B share companies listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, only China Merchants Shekou Port Service Holdings Co Ltd currently has a secondary listing abroad, in Singapore.
"This and three better-than-expected annual result announcements are likely to push up the B index in the near future," the analyst said.
Weifu Fuel Injection Co Ltd, Guangdong Provincial Expressway Development Co Ltd and China Vanke Co Ltd announced annual results on Thursday which brokers said were better than investors had expected.
But with many more B share companies still to release their results before the official April 30 deadline, investors will be reluctant to place heavy orders, traders said.
"The market mood is dominated by nervous optimism," a trader at China Guotai Securities said.
Livzon Pharmaceutical was the best performer on Thursday, rising HK$0.24 or 4.63 percent to HK$5.42 on volume of 108,100 shares.
Jiangling Motors Corporation was the next best, rising HK$0.14 or 3.80 percent to HK$3.82.
The A index slipped 4.15 points or 0.89 percent to end at 461.52 on turnover of 10.67 billion yuan after Wednesday sharp rebound which analysts said boosted Hong Kong's red-chip sentiment.
